claims.finding: blending of more than one SMG is a significant issue for single-dish surveys, more so for the brightest sources

evidence.quote: We detect more than one SMG counterpart in 34 $\pm$ 2 per cent of sub-millimetre sources, increasing to 53 $\pm$ 8 per cent for SCUBA-2 sources brighter than

claims.hypothesis: Are the ALMA counts consistent with the single-dish counts once boosting and blending are modelled?
claims.experiment: build completeness-corrected ALMA counts and compare to S2COSMOS end-to-end corrected counts and flux scales
claims.result: brightest ALMA SMG on average 1 (+1/-2) per cent lower than corrected SCUBA-2 flux; counts agree after correction
claims.finding: statistical corrections for multiplicity and boosting are reliable on average if the form of the counts is known

evidence.quote: showing that those statistical corrections are reliable on average, if the approximate form of the counts is already known

claims.hypothesis: Do physically associated SMG pairs make up a significant part of the multiples?
claims.experiment: compare observed multiplicity with unclustered end-to-end simulations; analyse [CII] kinematics of AS2COS 0001.1/0001.2
claims.result: ~30 per cent of multiples associated; 62 +/- 7 per cent chance for secondaries above 3 mJy; velocity separation 590 +/- 40 km/s at ~20 kpc
claims.finding: about one third of SMG-SMG pairs are physically associated, mostly the brighter secondaries

evidence.quote: these results indicate that $\sim$ 30 per cent of the AS2COSMOS multiple maps contain SMGs that are physically-associated

claims.hypothesis: Does the median redshift of SMGs increase with 870-um flux density?
claims.experiment: magphys photometric redshifts for AS2COSMOS combined with AS2UDS
claims.result: median z = 2.87 +/- 0.08 above 6.2 mJy; gradient 0.06 +/- 0.01 per mJy
claims.finding: clear evidence for increasing median redshift with flux, suggesting strong evolution in the bright end of the 870-um luminosity function

evidence.quote: Figure [9](#fig:photoz) indeed shows a strong trend of increasing 870-$\mu$m flux with redshift for the combined sample

why_this_data.value: retained targets with prior interferometric data to keep the survey homogeneous at 870 um

evidence.quote: To ensure that AS2COSMOS represents a homogenous study into the 850 $\mu$m-luminous population we retained these 45 targets in our ALMA Cycle-4 programme

why_this_method.value: Sersic profile adopted because comparable high-resolution SMG data are well described by it

evidence.quote: High-resolution ALMA imaging of comparable samples of single-dish-identified SMGs indicate that the observed 870 $\mu$m emission can be well-described by a Sersic profile

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Super-GOODS sample not used for the multiplicity comparison at matched flux limit

evidence.quote: We do not consider the Super-GOODS sample presented by (cite: Cowie18) as it contains only four SCUBA-2 sources with flux densities above the S2COSMOS selection limit.

limitations_admitted.value: multiplicity is a lower limit because the sample is very incomplete near 1 mJy

evidence.quote: our estimate of the multiplicity of SCUBA-2 sources is undoubtably a lower limit

limitations_admitted.value: observational constraints on projected versus associated companions are weak

evidence.quote: current observational constraints on the relative mix of projected and associated companions in blended SMG maps are weak

limitations_admitted.value: simulation-based line-of-sight correction assumes no clustering

evidence.quote: the statistical correction for line-of-sight multiplicity assumes no clustering

referee_caveats_inferred: The fraction of physically associated pairs rests on an unclustered simulation whose input counts model is itself fitted from these data, so the inference is partly circular.
Sample selection from a preliminary S2COSMOS catalogue plus archival fields of mixed depth makes the completeness correction (22 per cent at 6.2 mJy) significant for the counts normalisation.
Photometric redshifts and the flux-redshift trend depend on magphys settings that are only described in companion papers.
The 1.4-2.0x higher counts than AS2UDS are attributed to cosmic variance at only ~2.3 sigma.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Roughly 100-500 GB of raw measurement sets for the four Cycle-4 MSs plus seven archival projects; images are small (25.6 x 25.6 arcsec each, 0.1 arcsec pixels).
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA continuum steps (pipeline, tclean robust 0.5, taper to ~0.8 arcsec, SExtractor thresholds, Sersic uv-fit) and counts/multiplicity numbers are given with numeric results, but the parent catalogue, tclean details, SED-fit settings and several simulation details are deferred to other papers.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Archival projects are stated to be public and the continuum imaging, source extraction, flux fitting, counts and multiplicity recipe is largely complete with numeric answers; the SED/photo-z part is not self-contained.
